subject.title: MissingAgentHarnessError race: non-atomic harness registry clear+restore during plugin cache cycle

question: During empty-plugin-scope or plugin-cache reloads, which registered harnesses should survive: all prior harnesses, only core/bundled provider harnesses, or none with dispatch waiting/retrying until reload is ready?
rationale: The current source still proves the lifecycle hazard, but the durable fix defines plugin ownership and upgrade semantics for process-global runtime registry state, which automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Preserve core or bundled provider harnesses only
options.body: Keep critical provider-owned harnesses available across empty-scope reloads while still clearing third-party plugin-owned harnesses when their plugin is no longer active.

options.title: Restore every previous harness
options.body: Adopt the open PR's broader behavior and accept that explicit empty-scope activation can keep third-party harnesses alive until a later full reload clears them.

options.title: Clear harnesses and gate dispatch readiness
options.body: Keep empty-scope clears strict, but make channel/cron dispatch wait or retry on a named reload-readiness signal so users do not see transient missing-harness errors.

recommendation.title: Preserve core or bundled provider harnesses only
recommendation.body: Keep critical provider-owned harnesses available across empty-scope reloads while still clearing third-party plugin-owned harnesses when their plugin is no longer active.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice is mostly plugin/gateway lifecycle semantics, and this person has the strongest recent history on explicit plugin-scope and gateway startup registry behavior.
